caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1069 of 2009
lawyer:
A. J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, Instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Gias Uddin Ahmed, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent Nos. 1-9 & 15-16 
Respondent Nos. 10-14 & 17-21 ----- Not represented
parties:
Ramjan Ali Sowdagar and Ashraf Ali Khan Waqf Estate, represented by its Mutwalli Hajee Afazullah Khan ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Most. Ayesha Khatoon being dead her heirs Farukh Ahmed and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
"I have perused the materials on record, considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for both the sides and the statements of the witnesses. On further reading of the judgments of the Courts below it appeared to me that the petitioner as plaintiff in the suit in the trail Court prayed for certain relief in respect of the kabala dated 17/12/1972 and rectification dated 20/02/1975. The aforesaid suit was filed in 1975 which was disposed of in 1988 and, the appeal arose therefrom was dis-posed of in 2003 but in those long gap of period of 28 years the petitioner did not pray for framing an issue on the validity of the deed of gift meaning thereby he deemed to have abandoned this issue which can not agitated before this Division now. Further the petitioner also can not claim a relief in respect of deed of gift dated 26.04.1952 being barred by limitation because the limitation period was for 3(three) years only which was expired in 1955. But the instant suit was filed in 1975. The disputed deed of gift was not a void document but void-able as suit for cancellation has to be filed within period of limitation but after 1955 no suit could be filed. It also appeared from the record that Ramjan Ali Sowdagar purchase the suit land from Ombika Charan by registered deed (Ext-A) and he gifted the same to his minor Fazal Karim by deed of gift on 26.04.1952 (Ext-8) and thereafter Ashraf Ali Khan, the father of the petitioner acted as guardian of minor Fazal Karim who at his own will surrendered his guardianship by appointing one Moulavi Ahmed Sobhan by executing general power of Attorney (Ext-C) and Fazal Karim on attaining his majority recorded his name on the suit property (Ext-D) and thereafter assessment list etc. Fazal Karim also entered into an agreement for sale with Most. Ayesha Khatoon, registered on 27.10.1972 in which his father Ramjan Ali Sowdagar was witness (Ext-9). The above story testified that the suit property is owned by, the minor Fazal Karim presently major having deed of gift from his father on 26.04.1952 (Ext-B). Both the two courts below on fair assessment of the materials on record committing no error and carefully sifting the statements of the witnesses passed their judgments and decrees and found no illegality therein and as such there is no ground to interfere. The reference given by the learned Advocate for the opposite party has force and substance and are applicable in this case." 

 and that after attaining majority said Fazlul Karim, while in possession of the suit land, executed a deed of sale dated 17/12/1972 in favour of the respondent hereof transferring the suit land and in the said deed the original owner, donor of the gift, Ramjan Ali Sowdagar is a witness consenting to the said sale and thereby said Ramjan Ali Sowdagar is debarred from claiming the suit land in view of the principle of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel and that the Waqf being created, subsequent to deed of sale dated 17/12/1972, in 1974 the suit property cannot be included in the waqf estate legally and such claim is also barred by limitation, as has been rightly found by the High Court Division.
